title: Calypso Dx retail pilot integration notes
content:
Meeting summary and purpose:
- Call 2026-02-17 with Calypso DX (product + infra) to scope retail assistant pilot (POS / returns flow).
- Goal: 90-day pilot to validate latency and data isolation for transaction-enriched prompts; quantify per-interaction cost and UX regressions.

Attendees:
- Calypso: Nina Moreno (PM), Rajiv Desai (Infra), Sam Cho (Security)
- Redwood: Maya Chen (SE), Liam Patel (SRE), Sofia Rivera (Solutions Eng)

Business objectives (customer):
- Reduce agent-handled return triage time by 35% while keeping false-rejects < 2% (must preserve manual override).
- No customer PII leaves their AWS account; audit trail for every inference.
- Pilot must be demonstrably deployable to their VPC and support canary rollouts to 5 stores initially.

Hard constraints called out by Calypso:
- Must integrate with their on-prem POS fanout via VPC peering (no public endpoints).
- Egress bandwidth capped to 10 Mbps during peak; large-context examples must be clipped.
- SOC2 Type II + AES-256 KMS key usage required for any persisted caches.
- P95 latency target for single-turn return lookup flow: <=300ms end-to-end (including network to gateway).

Technical notes / brainstorming:
- Recommend Redwood Private (VPC) with per-store routing rules; use dedicated pool for initial canary to guarantee throughput.
- Use prefix caching for product lookup queries (short product vectors) and enable KV cache TTL of 30s for bursty traffic. Must confirm cache storage location: inside customer VPC vs Redwood-managed enclave.
- Consider quantized 4-bit variant for cheaper bulk inference on batched reconciliation tasks; keep fp16 for conversational prompts to reduce hallucinations.
- For PII handling, propose: 1) prompt-scrub pipelines running in-customer env; 2) store only de-identified metadata in Redwood metrics backend. Document architecture diagram needed.

Gotchas / unknowns uncovered on call:
- POS message size variability: some receipts embed base64 images; need clear rejection strategy or pre-filtering to avoid token blowup.
- Calypso's logging team wants full trace context tied to internal transaction id — confirm whether we can produce token-level cost data without including sensitive text.
- Their infra team has strict outbound IP allowlist policy; will require static egress IPs or a private endpoint.
- Regulatory window: in EU stores, they may insist on on-prem inference entirely; need to size a possible air-gapped package.

Immediate action items (owners + due):
- Rajiv (Calypso) -> share sample POS payloads (anonymized) and peak qps expectations by 2026-02-22.
- Maya -> draft architecture options doc (VPC peering vs private endpoint vs on-prem) and send to Calypso by 2026-02-24. Link: CONFLUENCE CAL Architecture stub.
- Liam -> spike static egress IP solution and map to Redwood Private onboarding checklist by 2026-02-26.
- Sofia -> create small eval prompt set (30 prompts) focusing on return-eligibility edge cases; baseline vs open-model and Redwood-verified model by 2026-03-03.

Testing & validation plan (sketch):
- Stage 0: offline evals with anonymized payloads (Sofia) — measure hallucination and false-reject rates.
- Stage 1: internal canary (5 stores) behind VPC peering, low QPS (10 rps) — test routing, audit logs, end-to-end latency.
- Stage 2: ramp to 50 stores, enable batching policies and KV caching, compare cost vs latency.

SLOs for pilot (proposed):
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn; p99 <= 800ms allowed for batch reconciliation.
- Availability: 99.5% over pilot window for canary pool.
- Accuracy: false-reject <= 2% on sampled human-reviewed set.

Risks / escalation path:
- If p95 cannot be met in Stage 1, fallback plan: route to lightweight rules-engine for 70% of traffic and reserve model calls for complex cases.
- If KMS integration timeline slips, pause any persisted caching work and rely on ephemeral runtime caches only.

Open questions (for next call):
- Can Calypso provide a minimal redacted dataset for benchmarking token distribution? (Needed to set batching and kernel selection heuristics)
- Do they require audit logs to include model outputs, or just metadata (prompt hash + decision)?
- For EU stores, are they willing to accept Redwood Private in a cloud region (customer-managed VPC) or must it be fully on-prem?

Notes to self (ramble):
- Keep the architecture doc modular; design for three deployment modes and call out cost deltas.
- We should prep a quantitative slide showing cost/latency tradeoffs for fp16 vs quantized variants for their workload.

Next meeting proposed: 2026-02-25 09:00 PT (technical deep dive with Rajiv and security).

Quick task list (short):
- [ ] Add POS sample files to secure intake (owner: Rajiv)
- [ ] Architecture options draft (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Benchmark prompt set and baseline runs (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Egress IP / private endpoint feasibility (owner: Liam)

End of notes.
